title: Computer Science and Computer Engineering for Games - Full Program Manifest
scope_note: Indexes the existing package. Module projects and Gates A-J are learner requirements, not completed implementations. The ten gates overlap module project briefs and are not 10 additional independent projects. External readings and extra problem sets are assigned, not bundled textbooks or fully authored exercise banks. This manifest does not change the original curriculum or archive.

volumes.title: Foundations and Your First Game
volumes.purpose: Learn to reason about programs, run code, debug, test, use Git and complete a tiny game.

modules.title: Starting as an engineer
modules.prerequisites: None. Basic reading, arithmetic and the ability to save a file.
modules.project: Create a learning repository with a working motion program, an environment record, a prediction table and a one-page explanation of the input-to-display path.

lessons.title: What a program actually does
lessons.outcome: Explain state, instructions, input and output using a tiny game.
lessons.practical_assignment: On paper, trace five commands: right 3, left 1, right 0, left 4, right 2, starting at x = 2. Draw boxes for input, simulation state and output. Save the trace. Pass: every state transition is explainable without running code.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: introductory functions/variables lecture; R15: Basics of Information.

lessons.title: Files, terminals and reproducible execution
lessons.outcome: Run a saved Python program and distinguish a shell from an interpreter.
lessons.practical_assignment: Follow START_HERE. Run the included program twice from the same folder; save the command and output in your journal. Intentionally misspell the filename, read the error, then repair it. Pass: you can explain which program produced the error.
lessons.assigned_reading: R04: Using the Python Interpreter; installation links in START_HERE.

lessons.title: Trace before running
lessons.outcome: Predict a program by following assignments in order.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create three assignment sequences with at least four statements each. Predict their outputs, then check with Python. Include one swap attempt that fails because it overwrites a needed value. Pass: fix the swap and explain the lost information.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: Functions, Variables; R04: An Informal Introduction to Python.

lessons.title: Units, budgets and engineering notebooks
lessons.outcome: Use units and simple arithmetic to check game calculations.
lessons.practical_assignment: Calculate travel at 2, 6 and 10 units/second for 0.1 and 0.5 seconds. Calculate frame intervals for 30, 60 and 120 frames/second. Pass: show units at every step and identify which assumptions are chosen targets.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: Variables and arithmetic; R15: Performance Measures.

modules.title: Values, decisions and repetition
modules.project: Build a terminal-based resource-gathering simulation with bounded health, inventory and a fixed number of turns. Include invalid-input handling and a complete trace for a five-turn run.

lessons.title: Types and expressions
lessons.outcome: Choose integers, real-valued numbers, strings and booleans appropriately.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write a resource-cost calculator that converts two text inputs to integers and reports total cost. Test zero, a positive count and malformed text. Pass: invalid input produces a useful message rather than an unexplained crash.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: Functions, Variables and Exceptions; R04: Numbers and Text.

lessons.title: Conditions and boundary cases
lessons.outcome: Write decisions with complete and non-overlapping rules.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a door requiring either a key or both level >= 5 and stamina >= 10. Enumerate all key/no-key cases around the two numeric boundaries. Pass: explain why each case succeeds or fails.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: Conditionals; R04: if Statements.

lessons.title: Loops and invariants
lessons.outcome: Use repetition that terminates and preserves a stated property.
lessons.practical_assignment: Simulate ten turns, collecting three units each turn and spending five only when affordable. Print a trace. Pass: exactly ten updates occur and the resource count is never negative. Add a test for zero turns.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: Loops; R04: for Statements and range.

lessons.title: Functions and contracts
lessons.outcome: Separate a calculation from interaction and state its valid inputs.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement advance with a documented nonnegative finite dt contract. Test stationary motion, negative velocity, zero dt and invalid dt. Pass: the function returns a value and the caller controls printing.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: Functions and Unit Tests; R04: Defining Functions.

modules.title: Organizing data and small programs
modules.project: Build a data-driven turn simulator with functions, a list of entities, a validated configuration file and save/load round-trip tests.

lessons.title: Sequences, dictionaries and identity
lessons.outcome: Choose collections according to the operations the program needs.
lessons.practical_assignment: Store five units with stable IDs, names and health. Look up a unit by ID and create a filtered list of living units. Pass: renaming a unit does not break lookup, and the original collection is unchanged by filtering.
lessons.assigned_reading: R04: Data Structures; R03: Loops and dictionaries.

lessons.title: Decomposition, modules and interfaces
lessons.outcome: Divide a small game into parts that can be tested independently.
lessons.practical_assignment: Refactor the resource simulation into simulation.py and a separate command-line entry point. Pass: importing simulation.py does not start a game or prompt the user, and a test can call its logic directly.
lessons.assigned_reading: R04: Modules; R03: Libraries and Unit Tests.

lessons.title: Files, serialization and validation
lessons.outcome: Save structured data without assuming every file is trustworthy.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create JSON save/load functions for a small state. Test a normal round trip, missing field, wrong type, unsupported version and truncated file. Pass: the original working save remains usable after a failed load.
lessons.assigned_reading: R04: Input and Output, json documentation linked from the standard library.

lessons.title: Classes, composition and state machines
lessons.outcome: Represent behavior without creating an unnecessary inheritance hierarchy.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a three-state character controller with a transition table. Pass: test every allowed transition and at least three forbidden transitions. Explain why composition would help add inventory independently of movement.
lessons.assigned_reading: R04: Classes; R03: Object-Oriented Programming.

modules.title: Debugging, testing and collaboration
modules.project: Publish a local tagged release of the terminal simulation with tests, a reproducible bug report, a reviewed change and an evidence-based development journal. A remote public upload is not required.

lessons.title: Debugging as an experiment
lessons.outcome: Find a defect by narrowing evidence rather than making random edits.
lessons.practical_assignment: Introduce a double-damage bug into a copy of the simulator. Write expected/actual behavior, reduce the reproduction and use a breakpoint or trace to identify the first incorrect update. Pass: fix it with a regression test.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: Exceptions and Unit Tests; R11: assertions and error-handling guidance.

lessons.title: Unit, integration and property tests
lessons.outcome: Choose tests that challenge the contract instead of repeating the implementation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write at least twelve tests across motion, resource spending and save/load. Include one property-style loop over many small inputs. Pass: temporarily insert a known bug and demonstrate that a relevant test fails.
lessons.assigned_reading: R03: Unit Tests; R04: unittest standard-library documentation.

lessons.title: Git, branches and recoverable changes
lessons.outcome: Use small commits to preserve reasoning and collaborate safely.
lessons.practical_assignment: Initialize the course repository, make three focused commits and implement one feature on a branch. Merge it and practice reverting an intentionally bad commit in a disposable copy. Pass: identify exactly what changed and why.
lessons.assigned_reading: R05: Getting Started, Git Basics and Basic Branching and Merging.

lessons.title: Review, documentation and responsible AI help
lessons.outcome: Explain a change and verify assistance without surrendering understanding.
lessons.practical_assignment: Review a ten-line change using a checklist: requirement, correctness, boundary cases, readability and tests. Write a README that a second person can follow. Pass: explain every changed line and recreate a small related feature without assistance.
lessons.assigned_reading: R05: Distributed Git; R11: philosophy and interface guidance; course assessment policy.

modules.title: A complete first game
modules.project: Complete Gate A: a deterministic terminal grid game with movement, obstacles, win/loss states, replay, tests and a clean-start README. Use the detailed project brief in the program handbook.

lessons.title: The update loop and command model
lessons.outcome: Separate simulation ticks from input collection and presentation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build a 10-by-10 terminal grid with one player and an exit. Pass: one command causes one update, drawing twice changes nothing, and the update function works without printing.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: runtime systems course overview; R27: fixed-step concepts, read without copying its implementation.

lessons.title: Collision rules and complete behavior
lessons.outcome: Specify edge cases before implementing a playable rule.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add five obstacles, a goal and a terminal win state. Test every edge of the board, blocked movement, reaching the goal and commands after victory. Pass: no partial movement occurs on rejected commands.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: game-programming projects; course transition and testing lessons.

lessons.title: Deterministic replay and simple measurement
lessons.outcome: Reproduce a run and measure the work actually performed.
lessons.practical_assignment: Save and replay a twenty-command session. Run the same replay repeatedly and compare final states. Time 10,000 headless updates separately from display. Pass: report exact inputs and no invented performance target.
lessons.assigned_reading: R27: reproducibility motivation; R04: time and random standard-library references.

lessons.title: Finishing, usability and the first portfolio artifact
lessons.outcome: Deliver a tiny game another person can run and understand.
lessons.practical_assignment: Complete Gate A and ask a tester to start from the README without verbal help. Record three observations and fix at least one usability issue. Pass: the tester can start, play, quit and rerun the tests.
lessons.assigned_reading: R29: Input, UI navigation and error-message guidelines; R05: tagging releases.

volumes.title: Mathematics for Games and Computing
volumes.purpose: Build the mathematical language for algorithms, graphics, physics, signals and experiments.

modules.title: Discrete mathematical reasoning
modules.prerequisites: Volume 01; complete the algebra diagnostic in START_HERE before proceeding.
modules.project: Write a mathematical notebook containing a truth-table specification, an induction proof, a graph model and a justified operation-count estimate. Include counterexamples to three false claims.

lessons.title: Algebra, functions, logarithms and trigonometry
lessons.outcome: Translate a game relationship into an equation with a defined domain.
lessons.practical_assignment: Solve distance = speed*time for each variable and state forbidden inputs. Convert 0, 90, 180 and 360 degrees to radians. Pass: solve ten algebra problems and explain logarithms using repeated halving before advancing.
lessons.assigned_reading: R08: prerequisite algebra review and trigonometric functions; R06: sums and asymptotics.

lessons.title: Logic, sets and quantified claims
lessons.outcome: Express requirements precisely enough to test or prove.
lessons.practical_assignment: Formalize five requirements for the grid game using sets and quantifiers. Construct truth tables for a door-access rule. Pass: provide a counterexample or witness for each negated requirement.
lessons.assigned_reading: R06: propositions, predicates, sets and relations.

lessons.title: Proofs, induction and invariants
lessons.outcome: Justify a program property instead of testing only examples.
lessons.practical_assignment: Prove the formula 1+...+n = n(n+1)/2 by induction. Then write an invariant for counting living units in a prefix of a list. Pass: show initialization, preservation and termination explicitly.
lessons.assigned_reading: R06: induction, invariants and proof methods.

lessons.title: Counting, graphs and recurrences
lessons.outcome: Model combinations and recursive work without brute-force guessing.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build a dependency graph for game startup and identify an invalid cycle. Count loadout combinations with and without a restriction. Pass: explain the recurrence for halving a search range and distinguish depth from total work.
lessons.assigned_reading: R06: counting, graphs, recurrences and asymptotic notation.

modules.title: Linear algebra and game geometry
modules.project: Build a tested vector/matrix library for a two-dimensional scene, then demonstrate a three-dimensional camera transformation with written coordinate conventions.

lessons.title: Vectors, dot products and projections
lessons.outcome: Use vectors for direction, distance and component measurements.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement length, dot and safe normalization. Use dot products to determine whether a target is in front of a character. Pass: test zero vectors, perpendicular vectors and opposite directions.
lessons.assigned_reading: R07: vectors and projections; R23: Geometry and Transformations / Vectors.

lessons.title: Matrices, bases and linear systems
lessons.outcome: Understand a matrix as a transformation rather than a table to memorize.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement 2-by-2 multiplication and solve two small linear systems by elimination on paper. Pass: show a pair of transforms that do not commute and explain a singular example geometrically.
lessons.assigned_reading: R07: matrix multiplication, elimination, inverses and vector spaces.

lessons.title: Homogeneous transforms, cameras and quaternions
lessons.outcome: Compose a scene using explicit coordinate conventions.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a parented object and camera using documented conventions. Pass: test identity, inverse round trips within tolerance, a translated direction that remains unchanged, and a parent rotation that moves its child correctly.
lessons.assigned_reading: R23: Coordinate Systems and Transformations; R19: geometric transformations.

lessons.title: Eigenvalues, least squares and singular values
lessons.outcome: Recognize stability and approximation problems in game data.
lessons.practical_assignment: Fit a line to five noisy position/time observations and report residuals. Analyze repeated multiplication by a diagonal matrix. Pass: distinguish data noise, poor conditioning and a programming error in your report.
lessons.assigned_reading: R07: eigenvalues, least squares and singular value decomposition.

modules.title: Calculus, mechanics and numerical simulation
modules.prerequisites: Modules 06.1 and 07.1; work through the linked calculus problem sets.
modules.project: Build a projectile and spring simulator with analytic comparison cases, timestep refinement, unit checks and a report separating model error from numerical error.

lessons.title: Limits, derivatives and rates
lessons.outcome: Connect derivatives to velocity, acceleration and local approximation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Compare analytic and finite-difference derivatives of three functions over several step sizes. Pass: include units, an error table and an explanation of why the smallest tested h need not be best.
lessons.assigned_reading: R08: differentiation, product rule and chain rule.

lessons.title: Integrals, accumulation and continuous probability
lessons.outcome: Interpret integration as accumulated contribution.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement rectangle and trapezoid integration for v(t)=2*t and a curved function. Pass: compare to an analytic integral, halve the step and report how error changes.
lessons.assigned_reading: R08: integration and the fundamental theorem; R23: Monte Carlo Integration introduction.

lessons.title: Newtonian mechanics and differential equations
lessons.outcome: Model motion from forces with clear simplifying assumptions.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a particle under constant acceleration and a damped spring. Pass: compare the constant-acceleration trajectory to its analytic solution and state what collision, rotation and air-resistance effects are omitted.
lessons.assigned_reading: R28: simulation, bodies, forces and impulses; R08: differential-equation applications.

lessons.title: Time integration, stability and error
lessons.outcome: Choose and test a numerical update rather than assuming smaller code is correct.
lessons.practical_assignment: Compare explicit and semi-implicit Euler on an undamped spring at three timesteps. Pass: plot or tabulate position and energy error, identify an unstable case, and avoid calling visual smoothness proof of physical accuracy.
lessons.assigned_reading: R23: physically based animation topics via R19; R28: simulation stepping guidance.

modules.title: Probability, statistics and evidence
modules.project: Create a reproducible benchmark experiment and a loot-distribution simulation. Report assumptions, uncertainty, representative workloads and one result that did not support the original hypothesis.

lessons.title: Probability and conditional reasoning
lessons.outcome: Model uncertainty without confusing independent and conditional events.
lessons.practical_assignment: Simulate independent and dependent binary events. Build a small contingency table for a hypothetical bug detector. Pass: calculate both P(alert|bug) and P(bug|alert) and explain why they differ.
lessons.assigned_reading: R09: probability, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem.

lessons.title: Random variables, distributions and sampling
lessons.outcome: Distinguish an expected value from a guaranteed outcome.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a weighted reward sampler and compare observed frequencies to the intended distribution over several sample sizes. Pass: record seed, generator, counts and expected values; explain finite-sample variation.
lessons.assigned_reading: R09: random variables, expectation and variance; R04: random reference.

lessons.title: Inference, uncertainty and benchmark design
lessons.outcome: Compare implementations without hiding variance or bias.
lessons.practical_assignment: Compare two implementations using the same inputs, randomized test order and repeated runs. Pass: report median, a tail percentile, sample count and limitations; distinguish observations from causal claims.
lessons.assigned_reading: R09: confidence intervals, hypothesis testing and experimental reasoning.

lessons.title: Regression, correlation and ethical telemetry
lessons.outcome: Fit a model while recognizing confounding and data limits.
lessons.practical_assignment: Fit a simple performance model using entity count and measured update time. Hold out some workloads. Pass: report prediction error and one confounder; write a short data-minimization plan for the experiment.
lessons.assigned_reading: R09: regression and inference; R01: ethics and data-management breadth.

modules.title: Signals, optimization and numerical foundations
modules.project: Complete Gate B: a mathematical engineering notebook plus tested transforms, numerical integration, signal filtering and an uncertainty-aware experiment.

lessons.title: Multivariable calculus and gradients
lessons.outcome: Use partial derivatives to reason about spatial fields and optimization.
lessons.practical_assignment: Derive gradients for three functions and check them with centered differences. Pass: test nonzero and stationary points, vary perturbation size and report errors rather than claiming exact equality.
lessons.assigned_reading: R07: linearization foundations; R23: geometric differential quantities; use the program's multivariable extension reading.

lessons.title: Sampling, aliasing and Fourier ideas
lessons.outcome: Explain why discrete samples can misrepresent a continuous signal.
lessons.practical_assignment: Generate low- and high-frequency sine samples, then downsample a checker pattern with and without prefiltering. Pass: explain the artifacts using frequency content rather than calling them random noise.
lessons.assigned_reading: R10: sampling and Fourier representation; R23: Sampling and Reconstruction.

lessons.title: Convolution, filters and systems
lessons.outcome: Predict a filter's effect on data and latency.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a one-dimensional convolution with documented boundary handling. Test an impulse, a constant and a step. Pass: predict the output before running and identify the filter's delay convention.
lessons.assigned_reading: R10: convolution, impulse response and linear time-invariant systems.

lessons.title: Optimization, conditioning and approximation budgets
lessons.outcome: Choose an objective and distinguish convergence from correctness.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement gradient descent on a quadratic and a two-variable problem. Pass: compare step sizes, record residuals and state a stopping rule; complete Gate B with no unsupported claim of global optimality.
lessons.assigned_reading: R07: least squares and conditioning; R23: numerical utilities; graduate optimization reading in the handbook.

volumes.title: C++, Algorithms and Language Implementation
volumes.purpose: Write native software safely, select data structures, analyze algorithms and build a tiny language.

modules.title: Native programming with C++
modules.prerequisites: Volume 01, Modules 06-07; do not skip the ownership module that follows.
modules.project: Port the deterministic grid simulation to C++20, with a command-line build, automated tests, warnings enabled and an explicit account of representation differences from Python.

lessons.title: Compilation, linking and build systems
lessons.outcome: Explain how source code becomes a runnable native program.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build the included C++ starter, then split one function into a header and source file. Pass: reproduce and explain one compile error and one link error, then restore a warning-clean build.
lessons.assigned_reading: R12: Getting Started and libraries; R11: Source Files.

lessons.title: Integer, floating-point and object representations
lessons.outcome: Choose native types with explicit range and precision assumptions.
lessons.practical_assignment: Print relevant sizes and numeric limits on the available compiler. Write checked conversions for a file length and tests for boundary values. Pass: do not trigger signed overflow as a test oracle; reject out-of-range input before converting.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: arithmetic and conversion guidance; R15: information encoding and arithmetic.

lessons.title: Values, references, pointers and lifetimes
lessons.outcome: Track where an object lives and how long access remains valid.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement functions taking values, const references and pointers with a documented null policy. Pass: explain each lifetime and identify a deliberately supplied dangling-reference example without executing undefined behavior.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: Interfaces, Resource Management and lifetime safety guidance.

lessons.title: Standard containers, iterators and error handling
lessons.outcome: Use library abstractions while respecting invalidation and failure contracts.
lessons.practical_assignment: Port the unit list to std::vector and implement lookup with an explicit not-found result. Pass: test empty input, missing ID and growth; document which operations invalidate stored references.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: standard-library use and error handling; R12: testing integration.

modules.title: Ownership, abstractions and C++ design
modules.project: Build a small resource manager with explicit ownership, safe move behavior, bounded interfaces, fault-injection tests and a written comparison of composition and inheritance.

lessons.title: RAII and resource ownership
lessons.outcome: Make cleanup follow object lifetime on success and failure paths.
lessons.practical_assignment: Wrap a mock file/device resource whose open/close counters can be inspected. Inject failure after acquisition. Pass: each acquired resource is released exactly once and no view outlives its owner.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: Resource Management and smart-pointer ownership rules.

lessons.title: Copy, move and exception safety
lessons.outcome: Define what transferring a resource means without duplicating ownership.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a move-only mock resource and transactional asset replacement. Pass: copying is prohibited, moving does not double-release, and injected load failure preserves the old asset.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: class special members, rule of zero and exception safety.

lessons.title: Interfaces, composition and polymorphism
lessons.outcome: Choose abstractions according to substitutability and measured cost.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create interchangeable console and recording renderers behind one small interface. Pass: both satisfy the same contract, tests run without display output, and ownership/destructor behavior is explicit.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: Interfaces, Class Hierarchies and composition guidance.

lessons.title: Templates, concepts and data-oriented choices
lessons.outcome: Use generic code without hiding costs or exploding complexity.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write a constrained generic clamp or interpolation function and benchmark two simple entity layouts. Pass: test contracts, record compiler/build mode and explain why the result is workload-specific.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: Templates and Generic Programming; R15: memory hierarchy motivation.

modules.title: Data structures and their costs
modules.project: Implement educational versions of a dynamic array, queue, hash table and heap, each with invariants and tests. Compare them to standard containers without replacing standard code in production merely for practice.

lessons.title: Complexity, arrays and linked structures
lessons.outcome: Predict asymptotic work while recognizing locality and constants.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a growable integer buffer for study. Count copied elements under doubling and one-at-a-time growth. Pass: derive the growth behavior and separately measure elapsed time without equating it to the proof.
lessons.assigned_reading: R13: arrays, cost models and asymptotic analysis; R06: sums.

lessons.title: Stacks, queues and ring buffers
lessons.outcome: Match ordering semantics to the intended workflow.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a bounded queue with explicit full/empty results and wraparound tests. Pass: preserve FIFO order through more than three times its capacity in operations and never read an uninitialized slot.
lessons.assigned_reading: R13: elementary data structures; R16: later concurrency comparison.

lessons.title: Hash tables and collision policies
lessons.outcome: Explain expected lookup behavior and its assumptions.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement chaining or open addressing with collision tests and resizing. Pass: deliberately force many collisions, test missing keys and verify that distinct equal-hash keys remain distinct.
lessons.assigned_reading: R13: hashing and dictionary data structures.

lessons.title: Trees, heaps and priority queues
lessons.outcome: Preserve structural invariants and choose the right query behavior.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a binary min-heap with push/pop and randomized comparison to a sorted reference. Pass: validate the heap invariant after every operation and test duplicate priorities.
lessons.assigned_reading: R13: binary search trees, balanced trees and heaps.

modules.title: Algorithms for maps, simulation and tools
modules.project: Build a pathfinding visualizer and asset-dependency planner. Provide correctness arguments, unreachable cases, complexity analysis and measured comparisons on multiple map families.

lessons.title: Searching, sorting and algorithm selection
lessons.outcome: Choose an algorithm from its preconditions and the data distribution.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement binary search with a documented interval convention and test empty, one-element, duplicate and missing cases. Compare two sorts on random and nearly sorted inputs. Pass: verify output order and element preservation.
lessons.assigned_reading: R13: binary search, sorting and comparison models.

lessons.title: Graph traversal and dependency ordering
lessons.outcome: Use graph algorithms with explicit edge semantics.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement BFS and topological sorting. Pass: recover a shortest unweighted path, report unreachable goals, reject a cyclic dependency graph and justify the O(V+E) traversal bound for adjacency lists.
lessons.assigned_reading: R13: graph representations, BFS, DFS and topological sorting.

lessons.title: Dijkstra, A* and admissible heuristics
lessons.outcome: Build a correct pathfinder before optimizing its queue.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement Dijkstra and A* against the same grid model. Pass: compare path costs on many small maps, include no-path cases and demonstrate a deliberately overestimating heuristic that can sacrifice optimality.
lessons.assigned_reading: R13: shortest paths; R20: game navigation context.

lessons.title: Dynamic programming, complexity limits and approximation
lessons.outcome: Recognize repeated subproblems and justify a practical solution.
lessons.practical_assignment: Solve a small 0/1 knapsack instance by exhaustive search and dynamic programming. Pass: compare answers, derive state count, and describe how a heuristic would be evaluated without claiming a guarantee it lacks.
lessons.assigned_reading: R13: dynamic programming; R06: reductions and asymptotic reasoning.

modules.title: Programming languages, compilers and computability
modules.project: Complete Gate C: a tested C++ simulation plus a tiny expression language with lexer, parser, evaluator, bytecode execution and resource limits.

lessons.title: Language paradigms and type systems
lessons.outcome: Separate language semantics from syntax and implementation habits.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write one rule in imperative and pure-functional styles, then define a small typed C-compatible interface for a mock subsystem. Pass: state allocation ownership and reject type-invalid expressions in a toy checker.
lessons.assigned_reading: R14: language frontend concepts; R11: interfaces and C-style boundary guidance.

lessons.title: Lexing, parsing and syntax trees
lessons.outcome: Convert source text into a structured representation with diagnostics.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement tokens, recursive-descent parsing and evaluation for numbers, parentheses and four arithmetic operators. Pass: test precedence, associativity, malformed input, unknown names and division-by-zero policy.
lessons.assigned_reading: R14: Kaleidoscope lexer, parser and abstract syntax tree chapters.

lessons.title: Bytecode, virtual machines and bounded execution
lessons.outcome: Implement a small execution model with explicit limits.
lessons.practical_assignment: Compile the expression language into stack bytecode and compare results to the tree evaluator. Pass: reject stack underflow, invalid opcodes and over-budget execution; preserve source context for errors.
lessons.assigned_reading: R14: code generation and execution concepts; course security requirements.

lessons.title: Automata, computability and compiler optimization
lessons.outcome: Know what analysis can establish and when transformation is legal.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add constant folding to the toy compiler and test it against the unoptimized evaluator. Pass: include a finite-state recognizer, explain a termination restriction and document transformations deliberately excluded for semantic reasons.
lessons.assigned_reading: R14: optimizer support; R06: computation models and proof limitations.

volumes.title: Computer Systems and Software Engineering
volumes.purpose: Connect programs to processors, operating systems, concurrency, networks, storage and professional practice.

modules.title: Processor architecture and assembly
modules.project: Trace a compiled C++ loop through a small assembly example and a cache model. Deliver an instruction/data-flow explanation and a controlled locality experiment.

lessons.title: Instruction sets, registers and calling conventions
lessons.outcome: Read a small machine-level routine without confusing ISA and implementation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Annotate a ten-to-twenty-instruction routine with register meanings and memory accesses. Pass: predict its output for two inputs and identify caller/callee responsibilities from the chosen ABI reference.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: Assembly Language and Procedures and Stacks; R35: selected base integer ISA.

lessons.title: Pipelines, dependencies and branch prediction
lessons.outcome: Explain why instruction count alone does not predict latency.
lessons.practical_assignment: Compare dependent and independent arithmetic loops while preventing dead-code elimination. Pass: preserve observable results, inspect generated code and explain measured differences as evidence rather than universal CPU facts.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: Pipelining and Performance Measures.

lessons.title: Caches, locality and memory hierarchy
lessons.outcome: Relate access patterns to cache lines and working sets.
lessons.practical_assignment: Benchmark sequential, strided and randomized access over multiple array sizes. Pass: record assumed versus measured hardware information and explain spatial locality without claiming exact cache behavior from one timing curve.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: Caches and the Memory Hierarchy.

lessons.title: Virtual memory, SIMD and architectural limits
lessons.outcome: Recognize address translation and vector execution as separate mechanisms.
lessons.practical_assignment: Inspect compiler vectorization reports for a simple loop and compare aligned/misaligned or tail cases safely. Pass: test lengths 0, 1, lane_width-1 and lane_width+1 and explain translation versus caching.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: Virtual Memory and Parallel Processing; R11: bounds and arithmetic contracts.

modules.title: Operating systems and resource management
modules.project: Create a systems lab report covering processes, memory, scheduling and file I/O. Use unprivileged programs and disposable data; do not alter kernel or device settings on a primary machine.

lessons.title: Processes, threads, system calls and protection
lessons.outcome: Explain which resources are isolated and which are shared.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write a program that reports its process identity and runs independent worker tasks. Pass: explain what memory is shared in the chosen approach and how worker failure is reported without privileged operations.
lessons.assigned_reading: R16: Processes, Process API and Threads.

lessons.title: Allocation, paging and memory-mapped data
lessons.outcome: Distinguish reserved address space, committed storage and live objects.
lessons.practical_assignment: Compare sequential file reads with a read-only mapped-file approach on a small disposable file. Pass: verify identical content and report virtual/resident concepts separately without promising one method is faster.
lessons.assigned_reading: R16: Address Spaces, Address Translation, Paging and Memory API.

lessons.title: Scheduling, responsiveness and real-time constraints
lessons.outcome: Distinguish average completion from meeting a deadline.
lessons.practical_assignment: Simulate a scheduler or instrument a bounded producer/consumer workload without changing privileged priorities. Pass: show one contention-induced latency spike and propose a structural fix rather than only raising priority.
lessons.assigned_reading: R16: Scheduling, Multi-Level Feedback Queue and Concurrency Bugs.

lessons.title: Filesystems, persistence and asynchronous I/O
lessons.outcome: Design data operations that survive partial failure.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build a save pipeline with injected failures before, during and after serialization. Pass: recover a valid prior or new save under your documented model and never reuse an asynchronous buffer before completion.
lessons.assigned_reading: R16: Files and Directories, Crash Consistency and Journaling.

modules.title: Concurrency and parallel programming
modules.project: Implement a bounded job system with dependency handling, shutdown, failure propagation and stress tests. Compare one-thread and multi-thread execution on a real workload.

lessons.title: Races, mutexes and happens-before
lessons.outcome: Protect shared invariants using a clear synchronization model.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a shared counter and a compound inventory transaction with proper synchronization. Pass: stress test, inspect with an available race detector and explain why detector silence alone is not proof.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: Concurrency and Parallelism; R16: Locks and Concurrency Bugs.

lessons.title: Condition variables, deadlocks and cancellation
lessons.outcome: Make waiting and shutdown correct under adverse timing.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a producer/consumer queue with graceful shutdown and failure propagation. Pass: test stopping with an empty queue, a full queue and active consumers; no thread remains blocked indefinitely.
lessons.assigned_reading: R16: Condition Variables, Semaphores and Concurrency Bugs; R11: locking guidance.

lessons.title: Atomics, memory ordering and false sharing
lessons.outcome: Use low-level synchronization only with a complete correctness argument.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write a publication litmus test with a documented happens-before diagram. Measure a padded versus unpadded counter layout. Pass: do not claim stress tests prove memory-model correctness or assume a fixed cache-line size without labeling it.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: atomics and memory model; R16: concurrency; R37: later GPU memory-model comparison.

lessons.title: Task graphs, work stealing and scaling limits
lessons.outcome: Parallelize independent work and measure end-to-end benefit.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a small task graph for independent entity updates followed by aggregation. Pass: compare 1, 2 and available worker counts, verify results and explain a case where more workers hurt.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: Parallel Processing; R16: concurrency; R11: task-oriented concurrency guidance.

modules.title: Networks, storage and data services
modules.project: Build a local-only client/server message exercise and a small relational game-data service. Test malformed framing, transaction rollback and duplicate requests without exposing a public service.

lessons.title: Network layers, latency and transport semantics
lessons.outcome: Choose transport behavior from application requirements.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a localhost client/server exchange with a length-prefixed message. Pass: split one message across several writes and combine several messages in one write; the receiver reconstructs them correctly.
lessons.assigned_reading: R17: TCP service and interface semantics; R16: networking context.

lessons.title: Protocol design, serialization and timeouts
lessons.outcome: Treat every received byte as untrusted structured input.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add versioned framing, maximum sizes, timeout handling and request IDs to the lab protocol. Pass: reject oversized and truncated messages before dangerous allocation and test duplicate delivery.
lessons.assigned_reading: R17: transport failure context; R18: transaction and data-integrity foundations.

lessons.title: Relational modeling, SQL and indexes
lessons.outcome: Represent game data with constraints that survive application mistakes.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a small schema with primary, foreign and uniqueness constraints. Use parameterized queries and inspect one indexed query plan. Pass: demonstrate rejected invalid references and compare a query before/after indexing.
lessons.assigned_reading: R18: tables, queries, joins, foreign keys and indexes via the linked manual.

lessons.title: Transactions, consistency and distributed failure
lessons.outcome: Preserve invariants when several operations must succeed together.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement an inventory transfer with transactions and forced failure between updates. Pass: verify conservation, rollback and duplicate-request handling; document what is not guaranteed across processes or services.
lessons.assigned_reading: R18: Transactions; R16: persistence and failure reasoning.

modules.title: Engineering practice, security and maintainability
modules.project: Complete Gate D: a reviewed systems application with a design record, threat model, CI-style local test pipeline, dependency inventory and an incident/recovery exercise.

lessons.title: Requirements, architecture and design records
lessons.outcome: Make tradeoffs explicit and trace implementation back to needs.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write six measurable requirements and two decision records for the simulation. Pass: every requirement has an acceptance test and each decision includes a rejected alternative and a cost.
lessons.assigned_reading: R01: Software Engineering; R02: engineering design and professional practice.

lessons.title: Defensive programming and threat modeling
lessons.outcome: Protect assets and trust boundaries before selecting security mechanisms.
lessons.practical_assignment: Threat-model the save parser and local service. Add bounds checks and a small malformed-input fuzz harness. Pass: cap work/memory, preserve useful errors and record residual risks instead of claiming complete security.
lessons.assigned_reading: R01: Security; R11: bounds/lifetime safety; R02: information-security breadth.

lessons.title: Build automation, dependencies and release discipline
lessons.outcome: Produce a verifiable artifact from a known source revision.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a local clean-build script that runs tests and produces a versioned archive plus manifest. Pass: run it from a fresh build directory and deliberately break a test to confirm the pipeline stops.
lessons.assigned_reading: R05: workflows and tagging; R12: builds and testing; R01: software engineering.

lessons.title: Ethics, accessibility, teamwork and sustainable delivery
lessons.outcome: Evaluate engineering decisions beyond code correctness.
lessons.practical_assignment: Run an accessibility review and a blameless failure retrospective on the project. Pass: identify at least three actionable changes, assign acceptance evidence and document third-party attribution honestly.
lessons.assigned_reading: R29: input, text, captions and UI guidance; R01/R02: professional and ethical practice.

volumes.title: Graphics and Game-Engine Construction
volumes.purpose: Build a renderer and a small engine instead of only learning an existing editor.

modules.title: From geometry to a software renderer
modules.project: Build a CPU renderer that writes a portable image file. It must clip geometry, rasterize triangles, resolve visibility and interpolate attributes correctly. Keep it as a reference implementation for future GPU work.

lessons.title: Images, color and coordinate conventions
lessons.outcome: Define the numerical and geometric meaning of an image buffer.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write a PPM image containing a gradient and coordinate markers. Pass: the dimensions, orientation and channel values are verified by tests, and a README states all coordinate and color assumptions.
lessons.assigned_reading: R19: image representation and transformations; R23: Radiometry, Spectra, and Color.

lessons.title: Projection and clipping before perspective division
lessons.outcome: Transform geometry without confusing visibility with division by depth.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement clipping against one plane, then the complete chosen clip volume. Pass: triangles crossing the near plane remain finite and correctly shaped, and tests cover points exactly on the boundary.
lessons.assigned_reading: R19: perspective transformations, clipping and the graphics pipeline; R23: Cameras.

lessons.title: Triangle coverage, depth and perspective-correct interpolation
lessons.outcome: Produce crack-resistant filled triangles with correct varying attributes.
lessons.practical_assignment: Render two triangles sharing an edge and a receding checkerboard. Pass: no cracks under the documented fill rule, correct overlap ordering, and a visible comparison between affine and perspective-correct texture coordinates.
lessons.assigned_reading: R19: rasterization, barycentric coordinates and texture mapping; R23: Sampling and Reconstruction.

lessons.title: Rays, intersections and acceleration structures
lessons.outcome: Build a second visibility method and compare its costs with rasterization.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement sphere or triangle intersections and a small BVH. Pass: accelerated and brute-force results agree within a defined tolerance over randomized rays, including misses and grazing cases; report build and query costs separately.
lessons.assigned_reading: R23: Shapes and Primitives and Intersection Acceleration.

modules.title: Explicit GPU programming and graphics APIs
modules.prerequisites: Module 21 plus Modules 18 and 20. Choose one compatible backend, not all at once.
modules.project: Implement a GPU backend for the reference scene. Query device capabilities, enable available validation, document the toolchain and handle resize and shutdown safely. A CPU backend remains a valid fallback while hardware access is arranged.

lessons.title: GPU work submission, resources and pipeline state
lessons.outcome: Separate CPU recording from asynchronous GPU execution.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a window or offscreen target and report supported capabilities. Pass: render a clear color, capture validation output and explain which objects belong to CPU recording versus GPU execution.
lessons.assigned_reading: R21: Introduction and Drawing a Triangle; alternatively R24 or R25 for one native platform; R22: SDL3 platform setup.

lessons.title: Buffers, shaders, layouts and resource binding
lessons.outcome: Match data representations across CPU and GPU boundaries.
lessons.practical_assignment: Upload a transform and vertex colors, then add a bounded compute operation. Pass: host/shader layouts are documented, a readback test checks results, and non-multiple work sizes remain correct.
lessons.assigned_reading: R21: vertex buffers, uniform buffers and compute; R37: execution configuration and memory organization, only for the optional CUDA route.

lessons.title: Synchronization, hazards and frames in flight
lessons.outcome: Express dependencies without serializing the entire renderer.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a compute-to-draw dependency and two reusable frame contexts. Pass: validation reports no relevant hazards and a stress test never resets a context still used by the GPU.
lessons.assigned_reading: R21: synchronization, frames in flight and resource transitions; use R24 or R25 equivalents for the selected backend.

lessons.title: Presentation, resizing and device capability policy
lessons.outcome: Treat the window system as a changing environment rather than a fixed image.
lessons.practical_assignment: Stress resize, minimize, restore and orderly shutdown. Pass: no stale size-dependent resources, no division by zero, and a readable capability report explains enabled features and fallbacks.
lessons.assigned_reading: R21: swapchain recreation and device selection; R22: window events; R24 or R25: presentation and resource lifetime.

modules.title: Lighting, materials and real-time image quality
modules.project: Create a material-and-lighting demonstration with a documented color pipeline. Compare image quality and frame cost at identical resolution and scene content; include reference images, not only attractive screenshots.

lessons.title: Radiometry, reflectance and physically based materials
lessons.outcome: Explain how lighting models approximate light transport.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement diffuse lighting and one documented microfacet model. Pass: test a constant environment, grazing angles and roughness limits, and state approximations rather than labeling any shiny shader physically exact.
lessons.assigned_reading: R23: Radiometry, Reflection Models and Light Transport; R19: shading.

lessons.title: Textures, mipmaps, filtering and tangent-space detail
lessons.outcome: Control aliasing while preserving the meaning of texture data.
lessons.practical_assignment: Render a receding textured floor with and without mipmaps and inspect a normal-mapped seam. Pass: report texture storage including mip levels and explain why non-color data needs its own filtering policy.
lessons.assigned_reading: R23: Textures and Sampling and Reconstruction; R21: texture images, samplers and mipmaps.

lessons.title: Shadows, light selection and rendering-path tradeoffs
lessons.outcome: Choose a lighting architecture from scene and bandwidth requirements.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement shadow mapping and compare a simple forward path with tiled light selection or a small deferred prototype. Pass: disclose buffer sizes, light counts, transparency limitations and measured frame costs.
lessons.assigned_reading: R19: real-time rendering and shadows; R23: Lights and Light Transport.

lessons.title: HDR, tone mapping, temporal reconstruction and validation
lessons.outcome: Separate display mapping from reconstruction and simulation correctness.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add exposure, a documented tone mapper and a basic temporal accumulation experiment. Pass: capture a camera cut and disocclusion test, show failure modes, and compare both still-image error and motion behavior.
lessons.assigned_reading: R23: Film and Imaging and Sampling; R19: anti-aliasing and image processing.

modules.title: Engine architecture, simulation and resource ownership
modules.project: Build a small engine with a fixed-step world, generational entity handles, explicit resource ownership and an inspectable task graph. Keep the game rules separate enough to run automated headless tests.

lessons.title: Fixed updates, interpolation and overload policy
lessons.outcome: Separate simulation time from rendering time and real elapsed time.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement an accumulator loop and inject long frames. Pass: simulation advances consistently under normal load, interpolation is bounded, and the overload behavior is tested rather than silently spiraling.
lessons.assigned_reading: R27: Fix Your Timestep!; R20: game loops and timing. Use the article as a starting model, not a guarantee of determinism.

lessons.title: Entities, components, handles and data-oriented storage
lessons.outcome: Design identity separately from memory location.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a small generational entity store with two components and deferred destruction. Pass: stale handles fail safely, iteration survives queued changes, and benchmarks include creation, deletion and common queries.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: game-state organization; R26: gameplay architecture for comparison; R11: lifetime and interface guidance.

lessons.title: Allocators, task graphs and frame-resource lifetime
lessons.outcome: Make temporary storage and parallel dependencies observable.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a serial-then-parallel task graph and a checked temporary arena. Pass: resetting live storage is detected in tests, dependency order is verified, and the critical path is identified from a trace.
lessons.assigned_reading: R11: ownership and concurrency; R20: engine architecture; R26: engine systems as a comparative implementation.

lessons.title: Subsystem boundaries, save formats and reloadability
lessons.outcome: Choose interfaces that make change and failure manageable.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add versioned saves and one reloadable asset type. Pass: old supported data migrates, malformed data is rejected without partial world corruption, and subsystem shutdown works after injected initialization failure.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: resource management and tools; R26: serialization and gameplay architecture; R11: interfaces and error handling.

modules.title: Asset pipelines, editors and an integrated engine
modules.prerequisites: Module 24 and the software-engineering practices of Module 20.
modules.project: Gate E: deliver a small 3D engine demonstration with an asset cooker, reproducible scene, inspector, save/load, diagnostics and a measured frame/memory budget. A second person must build and run it from the README.

lessons.title: Importing, cooking and content-addressed asset builds
lessons.outcome: Treat assets as compiled inputs with dependency tracking.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build a cooker for one mesh and one image representation. Pass: identical declared inputs reproduce the same result, changed settings invalidate the cache, and corrupted sources produce readable failures.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: asset pipelines; R26: asset management and content tools. Apply Module 20 dependency and provenance practices.

lessons.title: Streaming, residency and memory budgets
lessons.outcome: Load content without allowing asynchronous work to violate ownership.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a bounded streaming queue with placeholder assets and cancellation. Pass: a forced small budget produces graceful fallback, no use-after-free, and a report of peak rather than only steady-state memory.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: resource loading; R26: asset management, asynchronous loading and streaming concepts.

lessons.title: Editors, inspection and undoable commands
lessons.outcome: Make engine state understandable and safely editable.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a scene inspector with transform editing and a ten-command undo/redo test. Pass: invalid inputs are rejected, focus does not trigger unintended gameplay, and save/reload preserves committed changes.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: game tools; R26: editor and reflection concepts. Use a minimal UI toolkit appropriate to the selected platform.

lessons.title: Engine integration and reproducible demonstration
lessons.outcome: Deliver a small complete system whose limitations are measurable.
lessons.practical_assignment: Complete Gate E using the project specification in the handbook. Pass: another person follows the README, a headless test scene passes, all assets have provenance, and a limitations section identifies remaining correctness or performance risks.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: project completion; R26: profiling and engine architecture comparison; revisit Module 20 release and review practices.

volumes.title: Game Systems and Production
volumes.purpose: Add simulation, animation, audio, AI, multiplayer, accessibility and release discipline.

modules.title: Collision detection and physical simulation
modules.project: Build a deterministic test harness for a small physics scene, compare your simple implementation with a maintained physics library, and record precisely which physical and numerical assumptions differ.

lessons.title: Broad phase, narrow phase and geometric robustness
lessons.outcome: Separate possible collisions from confirmed contacts.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a grid broad phase and circle or box narrow phase. Pass: no true pairs are omitted compared with brute force over randomized scenes, and boundary-touching behavior is documented.
lessons.assigned_reading: R28: collision module, shapes and broad-phase concepts; R19: geometry and collision.

lessons.title: Rigid bodies, angular motion and collision impulses
lessons.outcome: Use conservation laws with explicit approximations.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement center-of-mass impulses and a simple rotational case. Pass: momentum is conserved in isolated tests within tolerance, static bodies remain fixed, and energy behavior matches the chosen restitution model.
lessons.assigned_reading: R28: rigid bodies, contacts and simulation; R19: physical simulation.

lessons.title: Constraints, iterative solvers and continuous collision detection
lessons.outcome: Explain where discrete simulation fails and how solvers control error.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a fast-projectile tunneling test and a short chain of constraints. Pass: a continuous or swept test catches the projectile, and a plot or table shows constraint error versus iteration count and timestep.
lessons.assigned_reading: R28: joints, solver settings and continuous collision; R19: numerical simulation.

lessons.title: Physics testing, determinism and engine integration
lessons.outcome: Validate simulation with invariants and adversarial scenes.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build a regression suite with replay hashes on one pinned environment, finite-value checks and analytic tests. Pass: failures identify the first divergent tick and reports distinguish same-machine repeatability from cross-platform determinism.
lessons.assigned_reading: R28: simulation, determinism and limitations; revisit Modules 08 and 24.

modules.title: Animation, audio and interactive timing
modules.project: Integrate an animated character or articulated object with event-driven audio. Demonstrate smooth interpolation, bounded audio work, adjustable sound categories and correct behavior when animation rate differs from simulation rate.

lessons.title: Skeletons, transforms and skinning
lessons.outcome: Compute hierarchical animation without mixing coordinate spaces.
lessons.practical_assignment: Animate a two-joint mesh or line skeleton. Pass: the bind pose reproduces the source geometry, weights are validated and a parent rotation moves descendants consistently.
lessons.assigned_reading: R19: transformations and animation; R26: skeletal animation concepts.

lessons.title: Animation blending, state machines and inverse kinematics
lessons.outcome: Coordinate authored motion with runtime goals.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build idle/walk/action transitions and a two-link IK demonstration. Pass: interruptions behave as specified, unreachable targets are handled, and root-motion ownership is documented.
lessons.assigned_reading: R19: animation and inverse kinematics; R26: animation blueprints and blending concepts, compared with your own small implementation.

lessons.title: Digital audio, mixing and real-time callback discipline
lessons.outcome: Generate sound without missing the output deadline.
lessons.practical_assignment: Mix two generated tones with adjustable gains using a platform audio API. Pass: no clipping under the documented gain policy, bounded callback work and a recorded underrun or deadline-stress test.
lessons.assigned_reading: R10 from Volume 2: sampling and filtering; R22: SDL3 audio; R20: audio systems.

lessons.title: Spatial audio, animation events and multimodal accessibility
lessons.outcome: Synchronize feedback while preserving user control.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add spatial panning, separate music/effects controls and a visual equivalent for a critical audio cue. Pass: replay does not duplicate one-shot events and a muted-audio test still allows the required task.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: audio and event systems; R22: audio interfaces; R29 from the resource directory: audio and subtitle accessibility.

modules.title: Game AI, decision systems and machine learning
modules.project: Build an inspectable agent that navigates, chooses actions and recovers from blocked plans. Compare a rules-based baseline with one small learned or search-based component; evaluate behavior and runtime cost, not only win rate.

lessons.title: Navigation graphs, steering and dynamic obstacles
lessons.outcome: Separate finding a route from executing movement.
lessons.practical_assignment: Combine A* with a steering controller and a blocked-path detector. Pass: agent size is respected, unreachable goals terminate or report failure, and repeated replanning has a bounded budget.
lessons.assigned_reading: R46: Search; R20: game AI and navigation concepts.

lessons.title: Behavior trees, utility systems and explainable decisions
lessons.outcome: Represent behavior so designers can understand its failures.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement either a small behavior tree or utility selector with a trace viewer. Pass: action cancellation releases resources and three induced failure cases produce understandable explanations.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: game AI; R46: agents, utilities and decision-making foundations.

lessons.title: Adversarial search, planning and simulation budgets
lessons.outcome: Trade decision quality against bounded computation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement minimax with alpha-beta or a small MCTS agent for a tiny game. Pass: legal moves are always returned within a defined budget or fallback, and evaluation includes multiple seeds and opponents.
lessons.assigned_reading: R46: Games, Minimax, Expectimax and Monte Carlo Tree Search.

lessons.title: Learning systems, neural inference and responsible evaluation
lessons.outcome: Understand learning fundamentals without replacing every subsystem with a model.
lessons.practical_assignment: Train a small classifier or value estimator on synthetic game data and compare it with a rules baseline. Pass: independent splits, error analysis, inference timing, reproducible seeds and a fallback behavior are reported.
lessons.assigned_reading: R46: Machine Learning and Reinforcement Learning; R47: linear models, multilayer perceptrons, backpropagation and generalization.

modules.title: Multiplayer simulation and online services
modules.prerequisites: Modules 18-20 and 24; Module 26 for physical interaction.
modules.project: Create a local two-client multiplayer demonstration with a network simulator for delay, jitter, loss, duplication and reordering. No public server or paid cloud account is required. Document authority and recovery rules.

lessons.title: Authority, prediction and reconciliation
lessons.outcome: Provide responsive local control without trusting arbitrary client outcomes.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a one-dimensional or grid movement server with client prediction. Pass: invalid movement is rejected and induced delay produces documented corrections without permanently diverging state.
lessons.assigned_reading: R17: transport semantics; R26: networking and multiplayer concepts; R20: networking in games.

lessons.title: Snapshots, interpolation, relevance and lag compensation
lessons.outcome: Manage bandwidth and latency while making fairness assumptions explicit.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add remote interpolation and relevance filtering. Pass: out-of-order snapshots are handled, missing baselines trigger recovery, and the report explains both visual delay and hidden-state exposure policy.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: networked game state; R26: replication and network smoothing; revisit Module 19 message validation.

lessons.title: Lockstep, rollback and deterministic replay
lessons.outcome: Choose synchronization around the game model rather than genre slogans.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement rollback or input lockstep for the tiny deterministic game. Pass: a delayed-input test converges, state hashes detect a deliberately introduced divergence, and audio or reward side effects are not duplicated.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20 and R26: multiplayer concepts; derive the implementation using Modules 18, 24 and 26 rather than assuming engine-specific guarantees.

lessons.title: Match services, identity, persistence and failure recovery
lessons.outcome: Design a small online service without treating it as part of the render loop.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build a local match registry and idempotent result store. Pass: duplicate submissions do not duplicate rewards, unauthorized edits fail, and simulated service loss produces a documented client outcome.
lessons.assigned_reading: R18 from the directory: transactions; R17: transport; revisit Modules 19-20 for distributed failure and threat modeling.

modules.title: Production quality and the undergraduate engine capstone
modules.prerequisites: Modules 21-29 plus Gate D software-engineering evidence.
modules.project: Gate F: release a small original game using your engine, with one complete gameplay loop, settings, save/load, diagnostics, accessibility checks, a tested distribution and a technical postmortem. Scope is judged by quality of evidence, not visual size.

lessons.title: Profiling, frame budgets and performance regression tests
lessons.outcome: Optimize measured bottlenecks without sacrificing correctness.
lessons.practical_assignment: Profile the capstone scene, optimize one verified bottleneck and add a regression benchmark. Pass: repeated before/after results, unchanged correctness and disclosed measurement uncertainty are included.
lessons.assigned_reading: R26: profiling and optimization; R45: sanitizer diagnostics; revisit Modules 09 and 18.

lessons.title: Compatibility, accessibility, localization and human testing
lessons.outcome: Test whether people can actually use the complete product.
lessons.practical_assignment: Test the game at two window sizes, with remapped input and an expanded pseudo-localized text set. Pass: no critical clipped controls, a muted-audio task remains solvable and observed usability issues are tracked.
lessons.assigned_reading: R29: input, text, audio, contrast and UI guidelines; R20: playtesting and production.

lessons.title: Packaging, patching, modding and supply-chain boundaries
lessons.outcome: Distribute a game without creating an uncontrolled execution path.
lessons.practical_assignment: Package the game and implement a data-only mod with a versioned schema. Pass: a clean-folder launch works, oversized or malformed mods are rejected and an interrupted-update simulation preserves a valid version.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: production; R26: packaging and plugins; R45 and Module 20: defensive memory and dependency practices.

lessons.title: Capstone review, release and technical postmortem
lessons.outcome: Demonstrate ownership of a complete engineering result.
lessons.practical_assignment: Complete Gate F and the oral questions in the handbook. Pass: another tester finishes a full loop, the release is reproducible, critical defects are resolved or clearly blocked from release, and the postmortem cites measured evidence.
lessons.assigned_reading: R20: course projects and critique; revisit the project rubric and professional-practice lessons.

volumes.title: Computer Engineering and Digital Design
volumes.purpose: Move from circuits and gates to RTL, a processor and an FPGA-based game subsystem.

modules.title: Circuits, measurement and electronic foundations
modules.prerequisites: Modules 06-10; basic algebra and calculus competence required. Simulation is the default laboratory.
modules.project: Create a circuit laboratory notebook using simulation first: voltage/current prediction, an RC transient, a transistor switch and a sampled input. Physical extensions require a qualified mentor and a documented low-voltage safety review.

lessons.title: Voltage, current, resistance and safe measurement
lessons.outcome: Analyze a simple circuit using units and conservation laws.
lessons.practical_assignment: Simulate a two-resistor divider and verify node voltages and current conservation. Pass: predictions include units, the source/load assumptions are stated, and a safety checklist precedes any physical experiment.
lessons.assigned_reading: R30: lumped-circuit abstraction, resistive networks and basic circuit analysis.

lessons.title: Capacitors, inductors, transients and frequency response
lessons.outcome: Relate stored energy to timing and filtering behavior.
lessons.practical_assignment: Simulate an RC step response and a sinusoidal frequency sweep. Pass: the measured time constant agrees with the ideal calculation within numerical tolerance, and the report distinguishes transient from steady-state behavior.
lessons.assigned_reading: R30: capacitors, inductors, first- and second-order systems; R10: frequency response.

lessons.title: Diodes, transistors, CMOS and analog interfaces
lessons.outcome: Understand the physical devices beneath digital abstractions.
lessons.practical_assignment: Simulate a CMOS inverter and one simple amplifier or comparator stage. Pass: plot input/output behavior, identify valid operating regions and explain one failure of the idealized model.
lessons.assigned_reading: R30: MOS transistors, amplifiers, digital circuits and operational amplifiers.

lessons.title: Sampling, ADCs, DACs and noisy controller inputs
lessons.outcome: Convert physical signals into stable digital measurements.
lessons.practical_assignment: Simulate a noisy joystick signal, quantization and a simple filter. Pass: report step size, calibration error, added response delay and behavior near the dead-zone boundary.
lessons.assigned_reading: R30: mixed-signal and measurement concepts; R10: sampling and filtering.

modules.title: Digital logic, state and timing
modules.project: Build and test an arithmetic unit, a finite-state controller and a synchronous queue model. For every block, provide a truth table or transition specification before coding its implementation.

lessons.title: Boolean logic and combinational building blocks
lessons.outcome: Translate a logical specification into a circuit with no stored state.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a small multiplexer, decoder and four-bit adder in a logic simulator or model. Pass: exhaustive truth-table tests cover every supported input and no state is required for a result.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: combinational logic; R31: Boolean logic and arithmetic projects.

lessons.title: Registers, finite-state machines and synchronous timing
lessons.outcome: Model state transitions at clock boundaries.
lessons.practical_assignment: Design a controller with idle, running and done states, including reset and abort. Pass: a transition table matches simulation and a timing worksheet includes setup and hold as different checks.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: sequential logic and finite-state machines; R31: sequential logic.

lessons.title: Binary arithmetic, fixed point and overflow policies
lessons.outcome: Choose representations that preserve the needed range and precision.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement wrapping and saturating addition plus a fixed-point multiply. Pass: boundary cases are exhaustive for a small width and an error report quantifies rounding behavior against a floating-point reference.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: arithmetic; R31: ALU construction; R35: integer arithmetic semantics as a software/hardware contract.

lessons.title: Clock domains, reset and metastability
lessons.outcome: Recognize where synchronous assumptions stop applying.
lessons.practical_assignment: Model a request/acknowledge crossing and explain its stability assumptions. Pass: the receiver never accepts a partially updated word in the protocol model, and the report states that simulation is not an analog metastability proof.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: synchronization and asynchronous inputs; deepen with R50 in later verification lessons.

modules.title: SystemVerilog and verification-driven RTL design
modules.prerequisites: Module 32; Python and C++ foundations complete.
modules.project: Implement a parameterized synchronous FIFO in RTL with a Python or C++ reference model, automated tests, assertions and synthesis reports. Keep testbench behavior separate from synthesizable hardware.

lessons.title: RTL semantics and synthesizable SystemVerilog
lessons.outcome: Write a hardware description rather than a sequential software imitation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a counter and two-register swap using a simulator. Pass: tests explain old/new values at each edge, lint warnings are resolved or justified, and no unintended latches are inferred.
lessons.assigned_reading: R32: language support, warnings and simulation; R33: synthesis concepts and supported constructs.

lessons.title: Testbenches, scoreboards and constrained stimulus
lessons.outcome: Check behavior against an independent specification.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a FIFO testbench with empty, full, simultaneous read/write and reset cases. Pass: an intentionally corrupted RTL version is detected, and a seed plus trace reproduces the first mismatch.
lessons.assigned_reading: R34: writing testbenches, triggers and simulator timing; R32: simulation and tracing.

lessons.title: Assertions, coverage and formal reasoning
lessons.outcome: Distinguish observed tests from properties proven under assumptions.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add occupancy, ordering and stalled-data assertions. Pass: bounded results state their depth, at least two meaningful cover goals are reached, and each environment assumption is justified.
lessons.assigned_reading: R50: getting started, FIFO example, safety, cover and liveness; R34: assertion-oriented simulation checks.

lessons.title: Synthesis, constraints and FPGA resource mapping
lessons.outcome: Connect verified behavior to a realizable implementation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Synthesize the FIFO and compare two storage implementations or depths. Pass: record device/model, tool version, inferred memory, registers and timing constraints; reconcile any post-synthesis behavior differences.
lessons.assigned_reading: R33: synthesis and memory mapping; R32: lint; selected FPGA tool documentation only after a target is chosen.

modules.title: Designing a small processor
modules.prerequisites: Modules 16 and 32-33. Implement a documented subset, not an unqualified full-ISA claim.
modules.project: Create a simple processor model and RTL implementation for a clearly specified instruction subset. Run the same short programs on an instruction-level reference and the RTL, comparing architectural state at retirement.

lessons.title: Instruction sets, datapaths and single-cycle execution
lessons.outcome: Separate programmer-visible behavior from its implementation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement arithmetic, load/store and one branch form in a reference model and datapath. Pass: hand-encoded programs produce the expected register and memory state and unsupported encodings have defined behavior.
lessons.assigned_reading: R35: selected base integer instructions; R15: processor design; R31: computer architecture projects.

lessons.title: Pipelining, forwarding, stalls and branch recovery
lessons.outcome: Preserve architectural behavior while overlapping instructions.
lessons.practical_assignment: Pipeline the processor or model a pipeline with explicit valid bits. Pass: dependent arithmetic, load-use, branch-taken and back-to-back memory tests match the architectural reference.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: pipelined processors; R35: instruction semantics; R32: tracing and debugging.

lessons.title: Memory interfaces, caches and protection boundaries
lessons.outcome: Design memory behavior as a protocol rather than an instantaneous array.
lessons.practical_assignment: Add a variable-latency memory model and an optional direct-mapped cache. Pass: randomized stalls preserve program results, each accepted store occurs exactly as specified and cache tests include conflicting addresses.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: caches, memory and I/O; R35: memory access and selected privilege concepts as an extension.

lessons.title: Processor verification, toolchains and architectural evidence
lessons.outcome: Demonstrate instruction correctness with reproducible programs and traces.
lessons.practical_assignment: Run at least twenty directed programs and a reproducible randomized set against the reference. Pass: mismatch localization works, binary layout is documented and a supported compiled or assembled program runs end to end.
lessons.assigned_reading: R35: exact chosen ISA revision; R32: simulation; R15: software/processor interface.

modules.title: FPGA-based game subsystems and integration
modules.prerequisites: Modules 21, 31-34. Physical deployment is optional; simulated I/O satisfies the core project.
modules.project: Gate G: demonstrate a verified RTL game subsystem, such as a sprite compositor, controller interface or bounded vector unit. Include a software reference, interface specification, automated verification and synthesis evidence. A physical board is an extension, not a prerequisite.

lessons.title: Memory-mapped I/O, timers, interrupts and DMA
lessons.outcome: Explain how software controls asynchronous hardware.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a simulated timer and memory-mapped control block. Pass: register side effects are specified, interrupts are acknowledged without losing new events and buffers remain owned until completion.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: I/O and interrupts; R35: ordering concepts for the chosen platform; R32: device testbench modeling.

lessons.title: Framebuffers, scanout and pixel pipelines
lessons.outcome: Produce timed pixel data with correct storage and scheduling.
lessons.practical_assignment: Create a simulated scanout counter and color-bar/sprite generator. Pass: exact active dimensions and frame boundaries are verified, captured images match the reference and buffer swapping occurs only at the declared boundary.
lessons.assigned_reading: R15: digital-system timing; R32 and R34: timed testbenches; use the selected board vendor's documented video reference only for a physical extension.

lessons.title: A small accelerator and its software contract
lessons.outcome: Measure whether specialized hardware improves a complete operation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Build a streaming arithmetic or pixel block plus a software driver model. Pass: outputs match the reference over boundary cases, backpressure preserves order and end-to-end cost includes setup and transfer.
lessons.assigned_reading: R33: synthesis and arithmetic mapping; R34: scoreboard verification; R15: parallelism and I/O.

lessons.title: Integrated digital-design review and optional board bring-up
lessons.outcome: Close the loop between specification, verification and implementation.
